thread:
maya: Anyone seen the Node SDK streaming client fail with CERT_VERIFY_FAILED when running behind our corporate proxy? Works locally but CI (linux Docker) gets 'UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY' when opening a streaming socket to streaming.redux.redwood.com

aj: Can you paste the exact error + the openssl s_client output if you ran it against the host?

maya: Error snippet from the app logs:
```
Error: unable to get local issuer certificate
    at TLSWrap.onStreamRead (internal/stream_base_commons.js:214:27)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:94:5)
Caused by: UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY
```
I ran `openssl s_client -connect streaming.redux.redwood.com:443 -showcerts` and it returned a cert chain where the issuer CN is `Corp Proxy Root` (so our proxy is MITM-ing TLS).

samir: Yep, classic corp MITM. Two main options: ship the corp CA into the container's trust store (recommended) or point Node at a custom CA bundle via NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. Avoid setting rejectUnauthorized=false.

jin: Quick notes: on Node, there are two common approaches
1) NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/corp.pem node server.js
2) programmatic https agent for SDK sockets:
```
const https = require('https');
const fs = require('fs');
const agent = new https.Agent({
  ca: fs.readFileSync('/etc/ssl/certs/corp.pem')
});
// pass agent into http/https client or SDK options that accept a custom agent
```
If you're using HTTP/2 / streaming, ensure the SDK uses that agent for the upgrade/stream socket.

maya: Is it safe in CI to use NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS? We don't control the runner OS image much. I could bake the CA into our Docker image but wanted a quick env override.

aj: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS is the easiest short-term. For Docker you can `COPY corp.pem /etc/ssl/certs/` and set ENV NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/corp.pem. For Ubuntu-based images you'll often also need to `update-ca-certificates` so system libs see it.

samir: FWIW the SDK has a config knob for TLS per-connection. Example (pseudocode):
```
redwoodClient = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY,
  tls: {
    caBundlePath: '/etc/ssl/certs/corp.pem',
    rejectUnauthorized: true
  }
});
```
But that only works if the SDK uses node https/Http2 options internally — we do for most transports.

maya: We thought about `rejectUnauthorized: false` to shortcut it — bad idea?

jin: Please don't. That disables cert validation and opens you to MITM in prod. Only ok for local debugging on an isolated env, but not CI or production.

maya: We also have a weird case with a customer that requires mTLS to the upstream and the proxy injects client certs. Any gotchas there?

samir: For mTLS you need the full client cert chain + key available to the process. With curl you'd do `curl --cert client.crt --key client.key https://upstream/`. In Node set `cert` and `key` on the https.Agent. If the proxy terminates TLS and re-establishes to upstream, you may need to provide client certs to the proxy instead of the app. Work with infra on that.

aj: Also check ALPN / HTTP2 — some corp proxies strip ALPN which causes the runtime to fall back to HTTP/1.1 and some streaming implementations expect HTTP/2 semantics. If you see protocol errors, that might be why.

dev-bot: Internal doc: https://redwood.internal/devex/proxy-ca-and-mtls (contains Docker image example, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, and SDK agent snippets).

maya: Awesome, i'll try baking the CA into our build and setting NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS for CI. Will report back. Thanks! :pray:

aj: 👍 keep us posted.

samir: ping if you want me to review the Dockerfile changes before merge.
